misconceptions.description: Assuming any group activity automatically produces deep learning
misconceptions.trigger: learner equates mere group formation with effective collaborative learning
misconceptions.feedback: Collaboration is not automatically effective. It becomes instructionally powerful when the task, roles, outputs, and support structures are intentionally designed.

misconceptions.description: Treating the ZPD as something only instructors can scaffold
misconceptions.trigger: learner excludes peers, tools, or systems from the support structure
misconceptions.feedback: The ZPD can be supported by instructors, peers, tools, and intelligent systems. What matters is calibrated assistance, not only teacher presence.

misconceptions.description: Assuming collaborative learning should ignore individual responsibility
misconceptions.trigger: learner argues that only the group product matters
misconceptions.feedback: Good collaborative learning balances shared work with individual accountability, reflection, and evidence of participation.
